measured_act_curve.cause: seq_length (spread at fixed length is 0.0 across 3 reps; mxaz straddle was mixing seq lengths, not run-to-run noise)

measured_act_shape.method: measure_act_curve.py (from gpu-sim-7uz2) run on the idle RTX 5090 at two contrasting shapes, d_ff/d=4 and batch 1 held fixed so the comparison is about SHAPE not size. Logs are the script's per-rep stdout lines (seq=... rep=... af=...).
measured_act_shape.caveat: neighbour occupancy was NOT recorded for these two runs (the mapping author's omission, recorded rather than glossed). Treat as shared-box data. Reproduce with occupancy recorded before quoting the short-sequence spread as tight.
measured_act_shape.finding: act_factor is SHAPE-DEPENDENT AT SHORT SEQUENCE and CONVERGES AT LONG SEQUENCE: 48% across shapes at seq 2048, 1.0-1.3% at seq 16384-32768. The single-curve simplification the error budget relies on is therefore VALID WHERE IT IS USED (the deciding cell N16_seq32768) and invalid at short sequences.
measured_act_shape.mechanism: At long sequence the activation term is dominated by real token activations (scaling with seq x d x layers), so the per-token-per-layer coefficient converges across shapes. At short sequence fixed overheads -- allocator behaviour, fragmentation, workspace -- dominate and are attributed to the coefficient, which is where the apparent shape dependence comes from.
